title: stark-attest aggregate verifier: a header depth of 65 or more makes a shift overflow and panics in overflow-checked builds
preconditions: A caller passes untrusted bytes to verify_aggregate
The build has overflow checks on (dev, test, fuzz, or a profile that enables them)
description: parse_header accepts a depth byte of 1 to 255 if the blob is long enough. verify_aggregate then computes (i >> k) with k up to depth-1 on a 64-bit index (aggregate_verify.rs:63), so k >= 64 overflows the shift. The module documentation says the function returns None rather than panicking (aggregate_verify.rs:21-22). A blob of about 2.2 KB with depth byte 67 and zero or small sibling nodes reaches that line.
impact: With overflow checks on, the verifier panics on a crafted blob instead of returning None. A plain release build of the stark-attest workspace does not panic (shift count masked, proof then rejected). No caller outside host tests and the fuzz target was found in the kernel, bootloader or shipped capsules, so no attacker route to this panic was shown.
scenario: An input starts with a 32-byte root and a blob with magic NZKAGGR1, count 1 and depth byte 67.
verify_aggregate parses the header, accepts it, and reaches the shift at aggregate_verify.rs:63.
In an overflow-checked build the shift panics.

steps: A fuzz run (ASAN build) over the stark-attest aggregate target produced 11 crash inputs with one root cause; the printed site is aggregate_verify.rs:63:46 'attempt to shift right with overflow'.
An independent check fed one 2235-byte input to the unmodified crate: dev profile panics (exit 101), release with overflow-checks=true panics (exit 101), plain release returns None (exit 0).

Not done: no booted kernel; no caller found, so reachability is not shown; the crash was not minimised below 2235 bytes; the pinned STARKs repository commit used by kernel crates has no verify_aggregate.

remediation: Reject depth above 64 (or above the log2 of a stated leaf bound) in parse_header, or use checked_shr. Regression test: feed the 2235-byte input and assert None.
